title: "Streaming Linux Log Files to Amazon CloudWatch"

You may want to centralize logs from your Linux servers into Amazon CloudWatch for monitoring, troubleshooting, or compliance purposes. This can be achieved using the CloudWatch agent.

## Installing the CloudWatch Agent

First, you'll need to ensure that your EC2 instance has an IAM role with the **CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy** attached. For on-premises servers, you'll need to create an IAM user with this policy and generate access keys. AWS-hosted servers should work out-of-the-box.

Once that's done, you can install the agent. On Amazon Linux 2, RHEL, or CentOS:

```bash
sudo yum install -y amazon-cloudwatch-agent
```

On Ubuntu or Debian:

```bash
wget https://s3.amazonaws.com/amazoncloudwatch-agent/ubuntu/amd64/latest/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb
sudo dpkg -i amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb
```

## Configuring the Agent

Next, we need to create a configuration file. Create the file at `/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json`:

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "metrics_collection_interval": 60,
    "run_as_user": "cwagent"
  },
  "logs": {
    "logs_collected": {
      "files": {
        "collect_list": [
          {
            "file_path": "/var/log/syslog",
            "log_group_name": "/linux/syslog",
            "log_stream_name": "{instance_id}",
            "timezone": "UTC"
          },
          {
            "file_path": "/var/log/auth.log",
            "log_group_name": "/linux/auth",
            "log_stream_name": "{instance_id}",
            "timezone": "UTC"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

You can add additional log files to the `collect_list` array. The `{instance_id}` placeholder will automatically be replaced with your EC2 instance ID. Wildcards are also supported in the `file_path` (e.g., `/var/log/*.log`).

## File Permissions

The CloudWatch agent runs as the `cwagent` user by default, so you'll need to ensure the log files are readable:

```bash
sudo usermod -aG adm cwagent
```

Alternatively, you can set `"run_as_user": "root"` in the configuration file if you'd prefer to run the agent as root.

## Starting the Agent

Once your configuration is ready, start the agent:

```bash
sudo /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl \
  -a fetch-config \
  -m ec2 \
  -c file:/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/etc/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json \
  -s
```

For on-premises servers, use `-m onPremise` instead of `-m ec2`.

You can verify the agent is running with:

```bash
sudo /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -a status
```

To ensure the agent starts on boot:

```bash
sudo systemctl enable amazon-cloudwatch-agent
```

## Example: Collecting Posit Workbench Logs

If you're running Posit Workbench, you may want to stream the application logs to CloudWatch. Here's an example configuration:

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "metrics_collection_interval": 60,
    "run_as_user": "root"
  },
  "logs": {
    "logs_collected": {
      "files": {
        "collect_list": [
          {
            "file_path": "/var/log/rstudio/rstudio-server/*.log",
            "log_group_name": "/posit/workbench",
            "log_stream_name": "{instance_id}-rserver",
            "timezone": "UTC"
          },
          {
            "file_path": "/var/log/rstudio/launcher/*.log",
            "log_group_name": "/posit/launcher",
            "log_stream_name": "{instance_id}-launcher",
            "timezone": "UTC"
          },
          {
            "file_path": "/var/lib/rstudio-server/audit/r-sessions/*.csv",
            "log_group_name": "/posit/audit",
            "log_stream_name": "{instance_id}-sessions",
            "timezone": "UTC"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Troubleshooting

If logs aren't appearing in CloudWatch, check the agent logs:

```bash
sudo tail -f /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/logs/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log
```

Common issues include permission errors (ensure `cwagent` can read the files) and IAM policy issues (ensure the role has `logs:CreateLogGroup`, `logs:CreateLogStream`, and `logs:PutLogEvents` permissions).

More information can be found here:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html
